chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sale of a sword decorated with silver for cash, so he said, 'There is no harm in it.' I asked him about the sale of deferred payment (nasi'ah), so he said, 'If he pays back the equivalent of what is in its silver [content], there is no harm in it, or he gives the food [commodity].'

key_terms.فِضَّتِهِ: Its silver (referring to the silver content/value)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a sword with silver decoration for cash and on deferred payment sales in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of selling a decorated sword for cash, reflecting the practical juristic needs of the Shia community regarding movable goods. It further elucidates the rules of *nasi'ah* (deferred sale) by permitting repayment in kind—either equivalent silver or food—thereby ensuring the transaction avoids *riba* (usury) through precise equivalence in quality and quantity.
